Also, if attendance is expected, is there a list of who is required, and a room?

If she needs certainty about attendance, the department's colloquium announcements or the organiser will have it; I can't confirm it for her.

Understood — thanks for checking. I'll take it as: the Colloquium is going ahead as published, but nothing official says Sarah is required, and you can't confirm attendance. I'll leave her Mon 12:30-14:00 where it is and ask her advisor. Nothing else from me.

The department office says: the Monday 13:00-14:00 Colloquium is going ahead as published (not cancelled or moved), but they have no attendance list and can't confirm whether you're expected — that's the organiser's or the colloquium announcements' call, not theirs. So nothing official requires you to move your Advisor 1:1, and I've left Mon 12:30-14:00 as it is. I've asked Professor Alvarez whether he expects you at the Colloquium; I'll tell you when he answers. If you want, I can also dig out the colloquium announcements to see what's on that day.

Hello — alvarez-agent here (Professor Alvarez's assistant). A question about the official schedule: the Monday 13:00-14:00 Colloquium — is it expected attendance for CSE graduate students, or is it optional/open? And if it's expected, which part of it (the whole hour, or a specific talk/segment)? One of his students, Sarah, is deciding whether she needs to move a standing 1:1 for it. Thanks.

Yes, please dig out the colloquium announcements and see whether I'm expected — that's the part I can't tell you myself. Leave the Advisor 1:1 where it is for now; I'd only move it if the announcement or Professor Alvarez says I should be at the Colloquium.

The Monday 13:00–14:00 Colloquium is on the official schedule as published — going ahead, not cancelled or moved. That's all I hold.

Whether attendance is expected for CSE graduate students, and whether the whole hour or a particular segment is the expected part, isn't in the schedule I keep, and I don't hold attendance lists or room assignments. I can't tell you who is required. Her advisor is the right person to ask — and I understand it's the same Sarah who asked me directly.
Thanks — that's clear: it's on the schedule as published, and attendance requirements aren't in what you keep. I'll take the "is it expected for his students" part to Professor Alvarez himself.
Agreed — that's the right person to settle it.

One question from a student, for your call: the Monday 13:00-14:00 Colloquium. The department says only that it's going ahead as published — no attendance list, so they can't say who's expected. Sarah (sarah-agent) has a standing Advisor 1:1 Mon 12:30-14:00 and wants to know whether you expect her at the Colloquium, and if so which part (whole hour or a segment), before she decides whether to move the 1:1.

Just tell me yes/no (and which part) and I'll pass it on. Her 30-min 1:1 with you next week is booked: Mon Nov 23, 10:00-10:30.
No — the Colloquium isn't a required event for my students, so I don't expect Sarah there. She should keep her 1:1 as it stands.
Got it — I'll pass that on: not required, 1:1 stays as it stands. Nothing else pending on my side.

Settled ✅ Professor Alvarez says the Monday 13:00-14:00 Colloquium is **not** required for his students and he doesn't expect you there — so keep your Mon 12:30-14:00 Advisor 1:1 as it stands. Nothing moved, and no further digging needed.

Your week now stands as: 1:1 booked Mon 10:00-10:30 (confirmed by his agent), everything else untouched.
Perfect, that settles it — thanks for checking. Nothing else from me for now.
Anytime — everything's in the calendar file, and I'll flag anything that clashes. Just write when you need something.
